skill.name: untangle-codebase
skill.description: Untangle a whole codebase in one pass, so agents working in it read less per change, break less without noticing, and debug faster.
skill.summary: Guide repository refactoring through dependency analysis, grouped redesign decisions, optional cleanup, and behavior checks.
skill.author: caldoai

security_audit.summary: All 29 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around examples, identifiers, and code fences. No evidence found of credential theft, data exfiltration, or prompt injection. One semantic risk concerns stripping function bodies without specifying a separate analysis copy, which could damage working source.

remediation.issue: The skeleton-generation tip does not require a separate copy before removing function bodies.
remediation.suggestion: Generate skeletons in a separate temporary directory without overwriting source files, and preserve all existing user changes.

content.user_title: Untangle Codebase Dependencies and Refactoring Decisions
content.value_statement: Scattered logic and hidden dependencies make routine changes harder to review and verify. This skill guides agents through structural analysis, grouped redesign decisions, and behavior checks.
actual_capabilities: Guides agents to identify hidden dependencies, unnecessary coupling, surplus code, and special cases.
Organizes proposed structural fixes above the problems they address in a decision log.
Asks users whether to include optional comment cleanup and test cleanup.
Directs agents to implement redesigns and remove special cases that become unnecessary.
Requests repeated subagent reviews and final checks that intended behavior remains unchanged.
Recommends dependency graphs and Git history as evidence for architectural decisions.
limitations: Provides written workflow instructions, not bundled refactoring tools, graph generators, or test runners.
Requires repository access and host support for tools and subagents to carry out the full workflow.
Does not guarantee exhaustive issue detection or behavior preservation; results depend on agent judgment and test coverage.
The skeleton-generation tip does not require a separate copy, so users should explicitly prohibit overwriting source files.

use_cases.title: Understand an Unfamiliar Repository
use_cases.description: Document hidden dependencies and misplaced responsibilities before proposing changes to an inherited codebase.

use_cases.title: Consolidate Repeated Behavior
use_cases.description: Group duplicated workflow logic and special cases under shared redesign decisions while preserving intended behavior.

use_cases.title: Review Architectural Boundaries
use_cases.description: Use dependency relationships and change history to assess module ownership and prioritize coordinated structural improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Start With a Problem Inventory
prompt_templates.prompt: Use untangle-codebase to inspect this repository. Complete the options discussion and problem inventory, then pause before implementation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: establish a reviewable baseline before changing code.

prompt_templates.title: Focus on One Area
prompt_templates.prompt: Use untangle-codebase on [area]. Keep comments and tests unchanged. Group structural fixes in a decision log and preserve behavior.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: limit refactoring to an agreed ownership boundary.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Shared Redesigns
prompt_templates.prompt: Use untangle-codebase to analyze [workflow]. Compare dependency relationships and Git history, then propose shared fixes for related problems before implementation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: investigate recurring changes across modules.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Controlled Refactoring Cycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Use untangle-codebase within [scope]. Preserve existing user changes and source files during analysis. Implement approved decisions in reviewable batches with regression checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: combine structural changes with explicit preservation constraints.

output_examples.input: Review duplicated action availability checks across a toolbar, menu, and command palette.
output: Problem: three interfaces maintain separate action lists and availability rules.
Proposed fix: define shared action metadata and behavior consumed by all three interfaces.
Verification: confirm each interface exposes the same actions and preserves existing availability behavior.

output_examples.input: Review dialog focus handling that relies on delays and global flags.
output: Problem: focus restoration depends on timing and coordination between dialogs.
Proposed fix: centralize focus restoration in the shared dialog lifecycle.
Verification: test nested dialogs and confirm focus returns to the expected control.

output_examples.input: Assess direct payment-provider dependencies in checkout and refunds.
output: Problem: checkout and refund workflows depend on provider-specific implementation details.
Proposed fix: define a provider interface for the operations both workflows require.
Verification: exercise each supported provider and compare observable behavior before and after refactoring.

best_practices: Agree on scope and optional cleanup choices before allowing implementation.
Preserve user changes, and create any analysis skeletons separately without overwriting repository source.
Review the decision log and run relevant regression checks after each structural change.
anti_patterns: Treating every special case as removable without checking the requirement it protects.
Removing comments or tests without the optional cleanup choice and a clear behavioral justification.
Allowing repeated whole-repository redesign without checkpoints, scope limits, or behavior verification.

faq.question: What does the skill actually provide?
faq.answer: It provides instructions for repository analysis, redesign, implementation, and verification. It does not include executable utilities.

faq.question: Which assistants are listed as supported?
faq.answer: The listing supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Tool availability and subagent support depend on the host environment.

faq.question: Can I focus on one area?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill accepts an optional area or concern, and your prompt can set explicit scope boundaries.

faq.question: Will it remove comments and tests automatically?
faq.answer: The instructions require asking whether to include each cleanup option. Test cleanup comes last because tests provide regression protection.

faq.question: Does it guarantee unchanged behavior?
faq.answer: No. It requires final behavior checks, but verification depends on available tests and agent judgment.

faq.question: What precaution matters when creating a code skeleton?
faq.answer: Require a separate analysis copy. The instruction to remove function bodies does not explicitly protect original source files or uncommitted changes.
